target_customer: Air travelers who want early warning of flight delays
problem: Airlines notify passengers of delays late; FlightCaster predicted delay probability hours earlier using historical data and live conditions.
business_model: Consumer mobile apps (iPhone and BlackBerry paid) plus a free website and an API

founders.name: Jason Freedman
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CEO. Education not stated.

founders.name: Bradford Cross
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CTO. Education not stated.

founders.name: Evan Konwiser
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Amex GBT among his affiliations; timing relative to FlightCaster not stated.

founders.name: James Bracy
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background.

founders.name: Jonathan Bracy
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background.

competitors.name: FlightStats
competitors.what: Flight tracking service, also a data source for FlightCaster

technical_complexity.rationale: Machine learning on ten years of flight data matched to real time FAA and weather feeds, run on cloud infrastructure, in 2009.

defensibility.rationale: A patent pending algorithm and historical models, but input data was public and tracking sites could add predictions.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it in the sources found; Next Jump acquired the technology and most of the team in January 2011.

market_need_then: Passengers faced frequent delays and the WSJ covered FlightCaster in 2009 as a way to learn of delays up to six hours before airlines notified them.

branding.domain_note: Used flightcaster.com; no purchase history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline style claim that it predicts delays hours before airline alerts.

branding.brand_signature: The weather forecast metaphor for delays: a forecaster for flights.
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by WSJ, TechCrunch, VentureBeat and travel blogs and discussed on FlyerTalk; no merch evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive and memorable name with good press coverage, but the user base was modest.

outcome_analysis: FlightCaster launched in 2009 with a delay prediction engine, raised about 1.3 million dollars in November 2009 from Sherpalo and Tandem, and was bought by Next Jump in January 2011 with undisclosed terms and the apps made free. Its technical edge and press coverage won an exit, while the small funding and paid app model suggest a modest consumer business; Next Jump wanted its technology and team for a travel product.
notes: The round investors come from CB Insights snippets and are unverified; the $1.3M amount appears in TechCrunch and VentureBeat headlines. Another source gives a total of $800,000, and CB Insights lists $1.32M over 3 rounds with a June 2009 seed, so earlier or later rounds may be missing. Competitor sources are a 2009 WSJ article reprinted by YC; FlightView holds a delay estimation patent but competition is not confirmed. Founder education not found. The YC page lists five founders; Konwiser's Amex GBT tie may postdate FlightCaster. Mentioning Bessemer or other names from my query is not supported.
